Bug_Details:
Use Random.nextInt(int).  Random.nextInt() % n can have negative results Random.nextInt() % n has a 1/n chance of being 0
a 1/2n chance of being each number from 1 to n-1 inclusive
a 1/2n chance of being each number from -1 to -(n-1) inclusive Many users expect a uniformly distributed random integer between 0 and n-1
inclusive, but you must use random.nextInt(n) to get that behavior. If the
original behavior is truly desired, use (random.nextBoolean() ? 1 : -1) *
random.nextInt(n).
Bug_Explanation: The bug occurs because Random.nextInt() % n can result in negative values, which is not expected if a uniform distribution between 0 and n-1 is desired. The correct behavior should use random.nextInt(n) to ensure values are uniformly distributed within the range.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBugTriggersBug method calls showBug, which uses Random.nextInt() % n, resulting in possible negative values. The assertTrue check fails when a negative value is returned, thus triggering the bug.
